correctness.rationale: The cited orthonormal monomial formula and compactness imply compact positive compound matrices. Every Cauchy minor is strictly positive, and after normalizing by the first k target monomial norms each compound row factor is log-convex and decreasing. Holder proves the operator-norm log convexity; the increasing order of output indices yields strict decrease. The bounded diagonal normalization converges strongly to the lowest compound coordinate; compactness upgrades this to norm convergence. Cauchy--Binet and the binomial kernel evaluate the limit as the square root of a positive finite moment Gram determinant. Ratios of successive limits give every fixed-index singular-value asymptotic. The standalone exact checker returned 4240 finite assertions; the analytic proof, not finite tests, establishes the infinite claims.

value.rationale: The theorem determines exact fixed-index approximation-number power exponents and positive leading coefficients for a natural recently studied two-weight differential Hilbert operator, beyond its known qualitative compactness/Schatten status. Its normalized exterior singular products have globally sharp determinant lower envelopes and a useful log-convex interpolation law in the target weight. These structural and quantitative facts address the natural next question after Schatten membership, and require infinitely many input coefficients but collapse to finite Gram determinants.
